summary: Motorcycles such as Pulsar, Chetak electric scooters and three-wheelers used to carry passengers or goods, sold in India and overseas.
description: Bajaj Auto develops and makes vehicles, then supplies dealers and overseas buyers. A motorcycle can take its rider to work; a passenger three-wheeler can be a driver’s way of earning a living. These buyers need different prices, features and support. Other companies in the reported group add lending, investment and overseas-brand activities.
money: Vehicle buyers and dealers pay for motorcycles, scooters, three-wheelers, parts and related offerings. Bajaj pays for components, batteries where needed, workers, factories, transport, marketing and repair promises. Group lending also earns interest but needs funding and repayments. Money received from these different activities is not all vehicle-sales profit.
customers: Dealers and overseas partners, followed by riders and commercial operators buying the vehicles. Group lending customers are borrowers who must repay loans; they are different from someone simply buying a motorcycle with cash.
drivers: Vehicles bought, models chosen, export demand, component and battery costs, discounts, service costs and the money needed by acquired or newer businesses.

groups.title: Motorcycles
groups.examples: Pulsar, Dominar, Avenger and commuter ranges.
groups.explanation: Customers buy transport for everyday trips or leisure. Engine size, features, price and running costs influence the choice; the most expensive model is not automatically the most profitable.

groups.title: Electric scooters and work vehicles
groups.explanation: The vehicle uses a battery and electric motor. A buyer considers charging and service as well as the price. The manufacturer must cover batteries, components and any repairs promised under warranty.

groups.title: Passenger and goods three-wheelers
groups.explanation: These can help drivers earn from carrying passengers or goods. A driver needs the vehicle to spend enough time working, with affordable fuel, loan repayments and repairs.

groups.title: Overseas sales and brand relationships
groups.examples: Exports and activities involving KTM and Triumph.
groups.explanation: Shipping Bajaj vehicles overseas, making vehicles under a partner agreement and controlling another company are different roles. The terms determine which work, costs and sales belong to Bajaj.

basics.title: Buying personal transport is different from buying a work tool
basics.text: An office commuter may value convenience and running cost. For an illustrative three-wheeler driver, fares or goods work must also cover fuel, maintenance and loan instalments. Their ability to earn can affect demand for new commercial vehicles.

steps.title: Plan the vehicle and obtain its parts
steps.text: Arrange designs, engines or motors, batteries where needed and the other components required.

steps.title: Build and test it
steps.text: Factories assemble vehicles and check quality. Production needs to match the models and quantities buyers want.

steps.title: Send it through the sales route
steps.text: Dealers or overseas buyers receive the vehicles under agreed terms. A vehicle sitting at a dealer is not yet a purchase by its final rider.

steps.title: Collect payment and honour support promises
steps.text: Sales must cover making and selling the product, repairs promised under warranty and other costs. Developing future vehicles and supporting group businesses may require more cash.

specifics.title: Export buyers face different local conditions
specifics.text: A dealer in one country may struggle to obtain foreign currency to pay for imports, while another market is growing. Import rules, loans and local conditions can therefore change orders separately.

specifics.title: An electric scooter must cover more than its battery cost
specifics.text: Sales must also cover other parts, staff, factories, selling, service and expected repair costs. Rising scooter sales alone do not show that all those costs are covered.

specifics.title: KTM adds a changed business boundary
specifics.text: The cited annual chairman’s letter describes obtaining control in November 2025 and work to improve the Austrian business. Group accounts combine controlled businesses; parent-only accounts do not include them in the same way. Compare the period included and the support needed.

watch: Are final buyers taking the vehicles dealers receive?
Manufacturer shipments can run ahead of rider purchases.
Read sales to dealers, final-buyer sales and unsold-stock commentary together. For exports, check partner orders and vehicles waiting in overseas channels where disclosed.
Which vehicles are changing sales and costs?
Motorcycles, scooters and work vehicles have different requirements.
Read what sold, selling prices, discounts, components and repair costs. Do not calculate a model’s profit from its price list.
Are export orders supported across countries?
One recovering market can hide weakness elsewhere.
Follow quantities, local demand, import rules and buyers’ access to currency. Distinguish a shipment delayed between periods from a lasting change in demand.
Are electric vehicles covering support costs?
Selling more vehicles creates future service commitments too.
Read battery arrangements, prices, service coverage and amounts set aside for expected warranty repairs. Separate achieved earnings from targets.
What cash and work does the KTM change require?
Buying control does not by itself fix a difficult business.
Read which companies enter group accounts, when their results start being included, and any loans, funding or unusual charges. Keep parent-only figures separate from group totals.
risks: Buyers cannot afford purchases or loans
Weak household or driver income can lead people to keep an older vehicle.
Currency shortages, import restrictions or transport problems can interrupt sales.
Electric vehicles cost more to support than expected
Battery problems, repair costs and price competition can reduce what remains from sales.
An acquired business keeps needing money
Improving a struggling operation may take cash and management time without an immediate recovery.
context: Electric scooter demand ran ahead of supply

Bajaj Auto’s 27 October 2026 standalone results release for July–September 2026 says Chetak electric scooter sales more than doubled from a year earlier even though supply was severely limited and demand exceeded what could be delivered; production is being increased. Standalone means Bajaj Auto Ltd itself, without its group companies such as KTM. The release says Chetak profitability kept improving but gives no separate Chetak profit, so none should be calculated from its sales. A shortage can leave buyers waiting or choosing another brand, and adding production costs money before the extra scooters are sold.
quiz: Can group sales growth be compared without checking which companies were included?
No. An acquired company can add sales and costs for only part of a year. Check the business boundary, dates and funding before judging growth.
sources: Chairman’s letter: KTM and business context

financialNotes.title: Use matching consolidation periods
financialNotes.text: The reported segments are Automotive, Investments and Financing, rather than one segment for each familiar vehicle brand. Segment income includes sales and other income; segment earnings come before the remaining financing and tax deductions. Read the reconciliation and the post-control KTM consolidation period before comparing years.
